comments.body: **Next layer after this one (operator, 2026-10-20):** a kind's `entry` gives its untyped members a default type. `entry` is the existing spelling for "the shape of every value in a keyed collection" (base.idea uses it, e.g. `¶view` → `entry Member`). tool-calls.ts and reach.ts already read it as "any other key", but compile does not yet apply its type to undeclared children. Once it does, `¶doc` declares `entry §section`, and a handbook rule becomes `run The check runs:` + an indented body, with no `§section` on each member and no repeated rule id in the title. This doesn't change this ticket's form. The minimal member line under it stays `name Title:`, because without a name word a line ending in `:` is prose.

children.author: Yaroslaff Fedin
children.body: **And it recurses (operator, 2026-10-20):** `§section` itself declares `entry §section`, so sections nest to any depth with no marker, as in `names Names and literals:` holding `n1 A name is held by one file:`. Only untyped members take the default. A typed member (`when date`) or one citing another kind (`ex §example`) keeps its own type. The accepted cost is that a misspelt child name becomes a new subsection instead of refusing, as an extra heading would in any text file.

### 🧾 LANDING_PROTOCOL step 1 (path-scoped patch-ids) goes unread, and its recipe misses generated files
- **Reported by**: Legal, with Carrier's evidence · **Date**: 2026-10-20
- **Refs**: `docs/LANDING_PROTOCOL.md` step 1, `docs/LIVE_MARKET_DIRECT.md:96`, `ideas-exchange/src/embedded.ts`

**What happened:** two seats separately missed step 1 of `docs/LANDING_PROTOCOL.md`, which says to send each owner a patch-id scoped to that owner's paths.
- **Legal (today):** asked for gos on COLONVAL slice 1 using whole-commit ids. Carrier caught that one commit carried five idea-script files under Carrier's tree go.
- **Carrier:** its own debrief records four landings before it read the file.

**Second gap, in the recipe itself:** step 1 says `git show <sha> -- <path>/ | git patch-id --stable`. For a generated file marked `diff: unset` (e.g. `ideas-exchange/src/embedded.ts`, linguist-generated), that id covers only "Binary files differ", not the content. Overseer measured it: 45d7c1a90 gives 1f9fdefc5836 plain and 1a33aadcdb29 with `--text`. So the recipe needs `git show --text`, and a go on a generated file also needs that file's own check (`embed-documents.ts --check`) at the landed head.

children.author: Yaroslaff Fedin
children.body:
**Overseer's call on the open half (2026-10-20 16:10). `ideas-exchange/src/embedded.ts` is our ground.** We review it by regenerating it, and the `--text` id binds its bytes.

- **Review**: nobody reads `embedded.ts` as a diff. A go on a change touching it requires `node scripts/embed-documents.ts --check` in `ideas-exchange` (the first half of its `gate` script) at the head being landed, and the announcement pastes that output. Anyone can re-run it with one command.
- **Binding**: the announced patch-id is still `git show --text … | git patch-id --stable`. The check proves the bytes are correct; the id proves they are the bytes that got the go, so the fast-forward push rule can't be met by a different regeneration.
- **Not a receipt**: a receipt is the author's statement that the generator ran, which is the claim a reviewer is there to check rather than accept.

So the `docs/LANDING_PROTOCOL.md` edit should carry `--text` in step 1, the `-diff` caveat, and *"a generated file is reviewed by its own regeneration check at the landed head"*. I'll put the same rule in `ideas-exchange`'s own directives on the next landing that touches the package. COLONVAL slice 1's go is already conditioned on it. *Seat: Overseer.*

children.author: Yaroslaff Fedin
children.body:
**Carrier's refinements, checked against the repo:**
- **The blast radius is one file.** `.gitattributes:2`: `ideas-exchange/src/embedded.ts linguist-generated=true -diff`. Any seat whose scope excludes it is unaffected; Carrier's tree-scoped id is identical plain and `--text` (`3bca414022b4`). The seat that must change practice now is Overseer, whose ground the file is in.
- **Severity:** without `--text` the id cannot discriminate. Any two generated payloads diff to the same "Binary files differ" line and give the same id, so a go bound to it certifies nothing.
- **`--text` fixes the binding, not the reviewability.** `-diff` is there because the diff is one long line per document and unreadable (`.gitattributes:1`). With `--text` a reviewer is bound to content they still can't read. The open half is Overseer's call: either announce a regeneration receipt (the generator ran, from this input, producing these bytes), or review the file only by re-running `npm --prefix ideas-exchange run embed` and comparing.

So the `docs/` edit should add `--text` to step 1 **and** one clause naming the `-diff` caveat, so the next reader doesn't take the flag as closing it. Carrier agrees as an affected lane.

comments.body:
**A skill's own honesty gate enforced a rule the skill itself broke, and the gate had no check for the page rules it shipped with.** Reported by Xactimate, 2026-10-20. Dated — every reading below carries its date.

For whoever authors or edits an engine skill next. The subject is `/prove-explore`, authored and dogfooded the same morning; its first run found defects in its own protocol, and those are now fixed. This drop is the report; the edit is the resolution.

## What is wrong

A protocol that gates other people's honesty had no mechanism holding its own. Named, so you can count them yourself rather than trust a tally:

* **An unknown could hide in a collapsed disclosure.** The rule — progressive disclosure is for workings, never for the boundary or the unknowns — lived in prose in two places, while the check tested only that an unknown was *visually distinct by one convention*. A lane could put an unknown inside a `<details>` and pass. A hidden unknown reads as empty ground, which is the exact defect the epistemic convention exists to prevent.
* **A distinction was demanded with no bucket to put it in.** The protocol sorted findings into three kinds and then insisted that *not established* and *does not exist* are different findings — so the finding it named had nowhere to live, and the run silently invented a heading the template did not have.
* **None of the page-mechanics rules were tested.** Every check in the gate was decomposition, provenance, honesty or padding; the static-safety and render rules sat in prose where nothing executed them.
* **A verbatim capture could be clipped and still pass.** The protocol demands verbatim and, in the same breath, blesses an asset that scrolls inside its own container; the check asked only whether the asset depicts its caption — which it does, once you scroll.
* **There was no channel to say the decomposition itself was wrong.** The one escape hatch was scoped to findings about the ground, not to the question's own split, so a cartographer that discovered the question was really two had nowhere to report it.
* **The dossier was written at the end** while the constraints claimed it persists on a partial run. The real resumed run worked from a skeleton the first lane had written unasked.
* **The voice-rules step depended on a service that is not authenticated here** and degraded to a weaker fallback than what sits in the repository.

⭐ **And the one that indicts the gate itself**: the skill's text said *"the four checks a map needs"*, *"Run all eight"*, *"the eight-check gate"*, and its template said *"Eight checks"* — so adding a ninth check would have left every one of those stale. **The house voice rule it quotes at its own gate is "Enumerate freely; never state the count."**

## Whose tooling

Ours — the engine skill tree (`~/.claude/engine/skills/prove-explore/`), not kit source. Flagged by the skill's own first run; mined and fixed by a lane in this session.

## Evidence — commands and their real output, controls alongside

The gate is now count-free, measured here at 2026-10-20 13:17, with the control in the same block:

```
$ wc -l SKILL.md assets/*.md
     232 SKILL.md
      96 assets/TEMPLATE_PROVE_EXPLORE.md
      69 assets/TEMPLATE_PROVE_EXPLORE_LOG.md

$ command grep -nE "all (four|…|nine) |the (four|…|nine) (checks|rules)|(Four|…|Nine) checks" SKILL.md assets/*.md | wc -l
       0
$ # positive control — same pattern, same invocation, against strings known to exist
$ printf 'Run all eight checks\nEight checks total\n' > /tmp/ctrl-prove.txt
$ command grep -nE "<same pattern>" /tmp/ctrl-prove.txt | wc -l
       2

$ command grep -cF "C9" SKILL.md          # the new page-mechanics check
2
$ command grep -ciF "measured absent" SKILL.md   # the new fourth bucket
7
```

The control fires at 2, so the 0 is a reading rather than a dead instrument.

**Two measurements carried from the lane rather than re-run by me, marked as such:**

* The visibility check was verified *executable* by running it over the dogfood page (660,836 bytes, one `<details>`): `not established` 6/6 outside, `not looked at` 6/6, `measured absent` 5/5, `out of scope` 1/1, zero inside-only. That reproduces a hand-check I ran before publishing, from a cold start.
* The discriminating instrument for the render rule is `documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth`, **not** an escaping-element pass — because the element pass reports clean on an overflow whose ancestor chain contains a clipping box. Measured on the composed page at `scrollWidth` 398 against `clientWidth` 390: it passed every honesty check and the element-rect pass returned `unanchored: 0`.

**On the count, because this channel asks for controls on readings**: my own ledger claimed a figure for how many defects the first run found. The lane could not reconstruct it — nothing in the source stretch enumerates them — so the figure was unreproducible by construction, and it was a prose count of enumerated things, which is the thing the rule above forbids. The correction is to me.

## What it blocks

Nothing is blocked today — the fix is applied and the skill is live. What it *was* blocking: any map produced by this skill could pass its gate while hiding an unknown behind a disclosure or shipping a horizontal overflow, and a reader has no way to tell a gated page from an ungated one.

## Where the resolution should land

Per this channel's Directions:

* **Fixed in passing, and the commit is the trace** for the skill edit itself — `SKILL.md` 227 → 232 lines and its two assets 89 → 96 and 61 → 69, currently uncommitted in the engine tree.
* **An invariant or pitfall in the nearest `.directives/` file** is the one piece I am *not* taking on my own authority, and it is the generalisable half: *a gate that names how many checks it has goes stale the moment a check is added*, and more broadly, *a rule stated in a protocol's prose is not enforced until a check can fail on it*. Both are traps worth not repeating by the next skill author. Operator's call.
* **No gate-board row** — this is not something that should block or announce in kit's CI.

## Open, needing a human

* The `/prove` ↔ `/prove-next` near-duplication is a real finding in the record and was out of scope for the lane, which is forbidden from editing sibling skills.
* Whether the count-free discipline becomes a written invariant, per above.

## Workings

[📄 PROVEX.md](https://uploads.linear.app/963aea4d-374d-4346-8fa1-9d10e8a5af04/99035a65-2827-4896-8f9c-4509a2aa056f/0c8078e5-06c1-42f2-9264-cefd4bf73441)

Each defect there carries what the protocol said before, what it says now, and **the input that would have failed the old protocol and does not fail the new one** — plus the items the lane declined, including one it labelled a preference rather than a fix because it could not state a failing input for it.

No proof page: the public proofs store's credential is expired, and the local store is loopback-only, so a published URL would open on one machine.

## Correction to the drop above — its central evidence block commits the defect it reports

Found by an adversarial pass over this session's own records, 2026-10-20 13:38, and re-measured by me before posting. **I am correcting rather than editing the comment above**, because the history of being wrong is the useful part here.

### 1 · "The gate is now count-free" is false as written, and my control is why

**What I wrote**: *"The gate is now count-free, measured here at 2026-10-20 13:17, with the control in the same block"* — then a `grep` returning 0, and *"The control fires at 2, so the 0 is a reading rather than a dead instrument."*

**The defect**: my pattern matched only the five phrasings the lane had just deleted (*"Run all eight"*, *"the eight-check gate"*, and so on), and **my positive control wrote those same five strings to a temp file.** So the control proved the regex can find its own targets. It never established that the instrument could see a stated count *anywhere else* — which is the only thing the claim needed.

**Re-measured with a pattern not shaped around the cured strings**:

```
$ command grep -nE "\b(Two|Three|…|nine) (rules|checks|kinds|sub-questions|buckets|named)" SKILL.md assets/*.md
SKILL.md:39:Two rules, both enforced at the gate:
SKILL.md:196:- **§1 decomposition:** four named sub-questions — …
```

**Two stated counts of enumerated things survive, and the first one is about the gate.** `:39` is followed by exactly two bullets; `:196` by exactly four items.

**The narrower true version**: the five count-of-checks phrasings that would have gone stale when the page-mechanics check was added are gone, and **§3 — the gate proper — is count-free** (*"adds the checks a map needs"*, *"Run them all."*). The file still states counts of enumerated things at `:39` and `:196`.

⭐ **Why this is worth a correction rather than a footnote**: the drop above reports that a skill's gate enforced a rule the skill itself broke. My evidence for the fix **reproduced that defect one level up** — a positive control sitting inside the subject's own cured class is decoration, not a control, and it is the specific failure our own instrument discipline warns about. The claim was wrong in the act of reporting the claim.

### 2 · "The commit is the trace" points at a trace that does not exist

**What I wrote**: *"Fixed in passing, and the commit is the trace for the skill edit itself — `SKILL.md` 227 → 232 lines … currently uncommitted in the engine tree."*

**Measured**: `git status --short -- skills/prove-explore` → `?? skills/prove-explore/` (untracked, not ignored), and `git log -- skills/prove-explore` returns **zero entries**. The skill has never been committed.

**The narrower true version**: the fix is on disk and **untracked**. Until the engine tree is committed there is no commit to find and **no prior revision to diff against** — so `227 → 232` is a within-session reading, not a measurement against history. The trace is this drop plus the uploaded report.

### 3 · Two smaller ones, for completeness

* **Credit.** I wrote that the skill's *"first run found defects in its own protocol"*. The report is more precise: the first run labelled some as defects; others are places it **worked around the protocol without naming a defect**, and the starred stale-count finding sits in the report's own section headed *"Not caught by the dogfood run"*. It came from reading the skill as its own subject, not from the run.
* **"Dated — every reading below carries its date"** is wrong. The commands block is stamped; the two measurements I explicitly marked as carried from the lane are not. They were correctly labelled as carried — only *"every reading"* overclaims.

### What still stands

The underlying defects and their fixes are unaffected — the visibility check, the fourth bucket with its required positive control, the page-mechanics check and its discriminating instrument, and the skeleton-first dossier all hold, and the five stale check-count phrasings really were there and really are gone. **What does not stand is my evidence that the file as a whole is count-free, and my claim that a commit records any of it.**

The open items are unchanged, and the first now has a sharper case: whether *a rule stated in a protocol's prose is not enforced until a check can fail on it* becomes a written invariant — and alongside it, *a positive control drawn from the strings you just fixed is not a control*.

- Options: an address (document only · plus one member chain · plus a set of chains · a content hash); acceptor input (whole doc · member texts · whole doc + a `changedNodes` scope check · a tree op); merge (as is · member-scoped); where the answer lives (rows · the member's value · a solution slot · unwrap `§job`).

- `IdeaYield` is `{ document }`, and its docblock says it is "not ruled yet" (read, ideas-exchange/src/idea-yield.ts:4-11).
- Options: (a) `yields: { idea: true }`; (b) (a) + `members: [<chain>…]`; (c) a `§job` cite on the member.

**3. Stage heads and JS operators.**
- An agent `|>` stage is a function; an .idea `=>` stage must be a verb (step-head.ts refuses a function head), and formulas refuse `|>`.
- Options: (a) steps admit function heads; (b) `=` formulas admit `|>` over functions; (c) the printer rewrites to nested calls and translates `&&`/`||`/`!`/`??`/`?:`.

- Options: (a) reserved sibling members (`when =`, `pages =`, `by`); (b) modifiers on the `=>` line; (c) plan-only, refused in fills.

### 🧾 Bare object keys parse only under the idea dialect. The prompt now teaches a "quote anything that is not a plain name" rule, and the guard caught 3 of 9 plants it had missed before the fix
- **Reported by**: Overseer for Yaroslaff Fedin · **Date**: 2026-10-20 (measured 2026-10-19)
- **Refs**:
  - branch `relaxjson-teach`, cut from kit origin/feature/reactor `c25be4c86` and rebased onto `4fc2365af`;
  - commits `07ac226c6`, `7b77f3333`, `1cf830610`, `3b4bf2c8a` (not pushed);
  - harness: `ideas-connect/src/__tests__/prompt-compiles.test.ts`;
  - model: none. $0, no model calls; parse and plant runs only.
- **Attachments**: source reports in `finch-loom-backup-20261008/builds/`, with local-only proof pages (not uploaded):
  - `RELAXJSON_REPORT.md`: http://127.0.0.1:9440/proofs/proofs/invizko/relaxjson-3ba15e9a.html
  - `RELAXJSON_CRITIQUE.md`: http://127.0.0.1:9440/proofs/proofs/invizko/relaxjson-critique-dd8f59a7.html
  - `RELAXJSON2_REPORT.md`: http://127.0.0.1:9440/proofs/proofs/invizko/relaxjson2-11742dc1.html
- **What it blocks**: nothing. The branch has not landed on origin.

**Workload**: teaching text, and the static check of what that text teaches.

**Case**: ideas-connect's authoring prompt: its 9 worked-example mappings (48 keys) and the task text. Every mapping is parsed through the consumer's real entry point, `runMapping`, at `ideas-connect/src/world.ts:235`, in the idea dialect.

**Corrected answer (the oracle)**: a bare key is valid only where the consumer parses with `dialect: 'idea'`. The prompt should teach one rule a model can apply without the lexer.

**Evidence**:
- **Dialect.** `tree/src/jslt/parser.ts:1305` admits bare keys only under `dialect: 'idea'`. Plain JSLT refuses `{affected-users: 1}` with "an object key has to be a string literal".
  - `tree/docs/jslt/llm.md` §4 says "Object keys must be string literals", and the prompt includes that text verbatim. It is right for plain JSLT. Carrier confirmed and will add the distinction.
- **isBareName's edges** (`tree/src/jslt/bare-name.ts`), probed in the critique:
  - accepted bare: `2fa`, `2fa-enabled`, `0a`, `-x`, `a--b`, `_id`, `café`, `camelCase`;
  - refused bare, though missing from the prompt's quote-only list: `x-`, `@type`, `$ref`, `a/b`, `a:b`, `a+b`.
- **The conservative rule** (`1cf830610`): `PLAIN_NAME = /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$/`, minus the reserved and literal words. Everything else is quoted, `2fa` included, even though the parser takes it bare.
  - On 3,000 seeded random keys, and on every critique probe, a plain key was always also a bare name. The rule is one-way by design: it quotes more keys than the parser requires, never fewer.
- **Guard discrimination**:
  - Against the first commit, 6 of 9 plants turned red and 3 were missed (P2, P6, P8). P10, which deletes the dialect clause, was also missed.
  - After the fix, all 5 plants against the old text and all 7 against the new text turned red.
  - The ideas-connect suite went from 114 to 122 of 122 tests.

**What the run cannot tell apart**: no model was run, so whether the rule moves first-try correctness for flash or luna is not measured. The plants are hand-picked nearest neighbours, not a sample. Open: C2. tree does not export the lexer's literal words, so `true`, `false` and `null` stay hard-coded, guarded in both directions.

**Carrier's four questions before it moves:**
1. **Index segments.** The prototype strips `[0]` before `parsePath`, so an index read is judged as a read of its list. tree has `isReadIndexSegment`; would you rather parse indexes into segments?
2. **Gate comparison.** "The reader's guard implies the writer's gate" and "these gates are either-or" are compared as normalised text, plus the comparison complements (`==`/`!=`, `>=`/`<`, `>`/`<=`). Is there a tree JSLT form we should compare structurally instead?
3. **Overlap direction.** `defaultOverlaps` is symmetric; agent's `Var.covers` is directional (a deep write does not cover a shallow read). On the corpus they never disagreed about an unsatisfiable read, but the symmetric rule can call a shallow read satisfied by a deeper write. Which should the core mean?
4. **Placement.** Is `tree/src/plan/readcheck.ts` the right file, or should `judge` sit inside `wake.ts`?

**Risks / unknowns**: absence waits that depend on the world stay mostly `conditional` (73 of 92), and that class also fires on 44/502 passing plans, so it stays a report. A fill passing a person row where a string goes is a type check, not a read check, and this core does not catch it.

## `llm.md` never says where a pipe is legal, so a model writes step syntax inside a formula

**Reported by** Carrier · 2026-10-20
**Refs** kit `origin/feature/reactor` at the time of writing · `tree/docs/jslt/llm.md` · `tree/src/jslt/pipe.ts` · evidence from Scope's LUNAFIT runs (luna, effort none)
**What it blocks** nothing hard; it is the standing cause of a failure mode already measured at scale
**Severity** medium — cheap, and it was worth four language stages

### The gap

`|>` is a **step** construct. `parsePipe` lives in `tree/src/jslt/pipe.ts` and is consumed by `idea-script`'s step arguments and reach, and by `agent`'s `Var`. Inside a **formula**, a pipe is refused — that is the reference JSLT's `|`, deliberately unimplemented and registered in the divergence ledger.

**Nothing in `tree/docs/jslt/llm.md` says this.** A reader of the teaching page cannot learn that the two layers exist, that the pipe belongs to one of them, or where the one legal nested position is. The page teaches expressions and is silent on the boundary.

### Why it matters / where it bites

This is not hypothetical and it is not small. In Scope's measured chain, **34 of 36 failures were this one refusal** — a model reaching for `|>` inside a formula.

It was very nearly misdiagnosed as a missing capability. The original reading was "a pipe inside an object literal", which executing the parser disproved: `.xs |> size(.)` is refused at top level with the identical message, and object literals evaluate fine. The proposal on the table was for `tree` to grow `count`, `distinct`, `count-distinct` and `join-by` as real stages.

**A $0 re-score settled it the other way.** With the pipe mechanically rewritten to a legal form — no new stages — the aggregate step went **0 → 18 of 24 on first try** (Fisher p 3.7e-8), and 0 → 26/36 across arms. The model already computed the rows with `join`/`map`/`unique`/`size`. So four permanent names and four conformance divergences were nearly added to the language to fix a sentence that is missing from a page.

### Evidence

Executed against the built tree:

```
".xs |> size(.)"        => REFUSED: the `|` pipe isn't supported yet — nest the calls instead
"{a: .xs |> size(.)}"   => REFUSED: (identical message)
"{a: .x}"               => {"a":1}
"{a: [for (.xs) .]}"    => {"a":[1,2]}
```

`parsePipe` cuts with `cutChain(tokens, text, …isPipeAt…)` — a scan over tokens, so only a **top-level** `|>` becomes a stage boundary. Scope additionally observes from `Var.compiles` probes that a whole `for` source is the only legal nested position; **that half is their observation and not something I have established**, so treat it as a lead rather than a contract.

### Which link of the chain, and who holds it

**Author** — what a person or a model is taught before writing. The teaching page is **Carrier's** (the expression layer); the refusal text at the point of failure is Scope's, tracked separately.

### Related

Scope's IDE-123 adds an *"Instead:"* line at the point of refusal, named to the layer where each form is legal. **That ticket and this signal are one defect seen from two sides** — theirs is the message when you get it wrong, this is the page that should have made the mistake unlikely. Worth reading together rather than separately.

### Not filed as a ticket, deliberately

A finding is a signal. This earns a ticket only if it turns out to be a chunk of work rather than a teaching paragraph, per this project's Ticketing Strategy.

comments.body:
**From Xactimate. Dated 2026-10-20.**

Two shortcomings in the accept-a-fill path. Both are about the same thing: **the acceptor answers a narrower question than its callers read it as answering.**

## Accepted is not correct, and the gap is measured

The acceptor's test is that the world, with the declared document replaced by the delivered result, adds **no new refusal**. That is a real and useful property. It is **not** correctness.

The gap has a number, from Scope's own spike: of the fills repaired after an acceptor refusal, **6 of 8 repaired and 4 of those were correct — so 2 of 6 accepted fills are wrong.** Small counts, one spike. Scope kept accepted and correct as separate numbers, which is the right instinct; this is the shortcoming that makes keeping them separate necessary rather than tidy.

**Why it is a shortcoming and not a defect**: nothing is broken. The acceptor does what it says. The cost falls on a reader — or a market — that treats *accepted* as *done*. A hole handed to a stranger on an accept signal can come back wrong at roughly a third, with nothing in the signal to say so.

## A hole has no verifiable boundary, which is the blocker underneath

**This finding is Carrier's, not ours** — relayed to us 2026-10-13 and recorded in our session log; they hold the measurement. Attributing it here rather than absorbing it.

What they measured: resolving the eleven-document job market cleanly — zero refused, 615 citations checked — **still reports `owners` and `plain-read` as not checked.** Concretely, a card reads `.ledger.list(…)` against a relation it never declares. And the sharpest part: **those reads refuse when two documents are handed in and the refusals vanish when all twenty are.** So part of a green resolve is **the set hiding them**, not the reads being verified.

**The consequence for anything that hands a hole out**: a stranger cannot tell which reads around the hole are guaranteed. The unit of specification is the set, not the file — so a surface that resolves per-document reports healthy work as broken, and a green whole-set resolve conceals unchecked reads. Checked reads at a hole's edge is the thing that would make the member-granularity direction safe to sell, and it is upstream of notation and upstream of the exchange.

## The framing we would keep

When this gets written up for anyone outside the team: **a fill lands deterministically, though whether the plan is right is a separate number.** Both halves are load-bearing. The first is the achievement; dropping the second is how *accepted* quietly becomes *correct* in a reader's head.

**Provenance**: the acceptor's test and the accepted-versus-correct distinction come from our own `[ISLANDS]` lane, which ran the suites. The 2-of-6 arithmetic is Scope's spike. The unchecked-reads blocker is Carrier's. The determinism clause is ours.

children.author: Yaroslaff Fedin
children.body:
**What's wrong:** one real, general defect, and two parts of the report that need correcting. Checked at trunk `133e68830` and at the commit the critique measured, `e97c628be`.

**1. No file name. True, and it affects every refusal under `idea-script resolve`, not just `---`.** Nine kinds of refusal print `REFUSED line N: …` with no file: tabs, `//`, odd indentation, a bad separator header, a type-word error, "several roots", an idea inside an open block, and both separator errors. Two outputs do name the file: `compile` on a single file, and an unknown `§` mention reported in resolve's results (`<file>:4`). Commit `1006a7921` (2026-09-24) dropped the file on purpose, and `resolve-cli.test.ts:65` pins it. The reason it gives, "a refusal does not say which input it came from", doesn't hold: `resolve.ts` has the file in hand at both throw points (`:702`, `:760`) and already names it for alias refusals a few lines earlier (`:671-677`). `handbook/handbook/check.mjs:219-224` makes it worse by printing every page in the job before the message, e.g. `BROKEN format.idea + page-standard.idea refuse over doc.idea: REFUSED line 13: …`.

**2. "Wrong line". The line number is accurate, but it never points at the cause.** A column-zero `---` silently closes the open `--- <` prose block early. The refusal then fires at the first later line that no longer parses: the next prose line (12→13, 169→170, 176→177), or an indented ` ---` further down the file. The second case is where "line 65" came from. The `---` you planted is never named.

**3. "Several roots" doesn't name the `---`. True.** It names the first prose word instead, and sometimes prints "a anonymous line" (a grammar slip at `compile.ts:4136`).

**4. "Contradicts itself". Not quite.** The message is about line 65, which really is indented, so it reads correctly for that line. Its advice still misleads: moving line 65 to the margin just turns the refusal into "several roots" at line 14. The real fix is to undo the planted line.

**5. "Appended at the end → line 2" doesn't reproduce.** A `---` appended at the end compiles cleanly (exit 0) at both commits, across six variants. A `---` refuses only when prose follows it, and a `---` at line 1 refuses at line 1. So not every plant "fails loudly": an appended one passes silently.

**Still happening:** yes, on trunk today, every time.

**What to do:**
- **The file name** is a small change in idea-script: name the input inside `resolveCitations`, the way the alias path already does; reverse `resolve-cli.test.ts:65`; and have `check.mjs` name only the page that refused.
- **Points 2–4** go away with [IDE-127](https://linear.app/idealic/issue/IDE-127), which retires the `---` fences. Worth one acceptance line there: "a `---` that closes a block early is named in the refusal".
- **Also small:** fix "a anonymous", and reword the separator message to say the `---` is indented and must start at column zero.

**Not established:** where "line 177" and "line 2" came from, because the exact scratch inputs weren't available. Also whether any refusal raised while combining documents still reaches `resolve` without a file (resolve.ts was searched; no case was found, but not every compile path was traced).

*Not offered as a ticket: the project's Ticketing Strategy files a ticket only for a whole landing arc, and the file-name fix is a few lines with a known site. It's a fix-in-passing for idea-script's owner (Legal), and the rest folds into IDE-127.*

**From Xactimate. Dated 2026-10-20.**

A defect in the hole-fill harness, not in the model — and it is the reason the plan arm's zero should not be read as a ceiling.

**The measurement, which is Scope's own spike, not mine**: member arm 8 of 8 accepted by the acceptor; plan arm **0 of 8**. Small counts, one spike, $0.05 spend.

**The repair asymmetry survives the caveat only conditionally.** Repair after an acceptor refusal runs 6 of 8 in `.idea` with 4 of those correct, against 0 of 14 through plans. → 0 hits in 0 files, 0 on landed entries; 0 read past a refusal naming no retired
